blocks.passage:
A letter of credit is a promise made by a bank. It says: if the seller sends the goods and brings the right documents, the bank will pay.

Why is this useful? Because the buyer and the seller may not know each other. Without a letter of credit, they must trust each other completely. With one, they trust the bank instead.

It is one of the oldest and most used tools in international trade, and it still works very well today.

items.q: Who makes the promise in a letter of credit?
items.why: "A letter of credit is a promise made by a bank."

items.q: What must the seller do for the bank to pay?
options: Send the goods and bring the right documents
items.why: "if the seller sends the goods and brings the right documents, the bank will pay."

items.q: Why is a letter of credit useful?
options: The buyer and seller may not know each other
items.why: "the buyer and the seller may not know each other."

items.q: With a letter of credit, who do the two sides trust?
items.why: "With one, they trust the bank instead."

items.q: How does the text describe the letter of credit?
options: One of the oldest and most used tools, still working well today
items.why: "one of the oldest and most used tools in international trade, and it still works very well today."

audio.text:
You've never used a letter of credit before, so let me explain it in a simple way.

Imagine you're selling coffee to a buyer in another country. You've never met them. How do you know they will pay? And how do they know you will really send the coffee? Neither side fully trusts the other.

This is where the bank helps. The buyer asks their bank to open a letter of credit. The bank promises: when the seller sends the coffee and shows the right documents, we will pay.

So now you don't need to trust the buyer. You trust the bank's promise. You send the coffee, you take the documents to the bank, and the bank pays you.

One important thing: the documents must be exactly right. If a date is wrong, or a paper is missing, the bank can say no. So we always check the documents very carefully, word by word.

That's the whole idea: the bank stands in the middle, and both sides can do business with confidence.

items.q: In the example, what is being sold?
items.why: "you're selling coffee to a buyer in another country."

items.q: What is the problem the letter of credit solves?
options: Neither side fully trusts the other
items.why: "Neither side fully trusts the other."

items.q: What does the buyer's bank promise?
options: To pay when the seller sends the coffee and shows the right documents
items.why: "when the seller sends the coffee and shows the right documents, we will pay."

items.q: Why must the documents be exactly right?
options: If a date is wrong or a paper is missing, the bank can say no
items.why: "If a date is wrong, or a paper is missing, the bank can say no."

items.q: What is 'the whole idea' at the end?
options: The bank stands in the middle so both sides trade with confidence
items.why: "the bank stands in the middle, and both sides can do business with confidence."

items.q: A **letter of credit** is…
options: a bank's promise to pay if the right documents are shown
items.why: Letter of credit = carta de crédito.

items.q: The **beneficiary** of a letter of credit is…
options: the seller who will be paid
items.why: Beneficiary = beneficiário (o vendedor que recebe).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The bank will **___** the payment if the documents are right."
items.why: Guarantee = garantir.

items.q: To **issue** a letter of credit means to…
items.why: Issue = emitir.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A letter of credit builds **___** between two sides who don't know each other."
items.why: Trust = confiança.

items.q: "The bank **stands in the middle**." To stand in the middle means to…
items.why: Stand in the middle = ficar no meio, entre as partes.

items.q: "The buyer asks the bank to **open** a letter of credit." To open here means to…
items.why: Open a letter of credit = abrir/emitir.

items.q: "We check the documents **word by word**." Word by word means…
items.why: Word by word = palavra por palavra, com cuidado.

items.q: "If a paper is missing, the bank can **say no**." To say no means to…
items.why: Say no = recusar.

items.q: "Both sides can do business **with confidence**." With confidence means…
items.why: With confidence = com segurança.
